KRS 83A.040(1), published by the Kentucky Legislative Research Commission, states that a mayor is elected at a regular election and serves a four-year term that begins on the first day of January after the election. The official Fayette County Clerk recap sheets posted by the State Board of Elections show Lexington-Fayette mayoral contests on 2010-11-02, 2014-11-04, 2018-11-06 and 2022-11-08, which is a four-year cycle, and the cumulative report for the 2026 primary shows the next contest in 2026. A mayoral term that starts in January after each of those elections leaves this year without a regular mayoral election. The cycle is inferred from the statute plus the observed official election dates. It was not read from a Lexington charter or a clerk list of elections, which could not be opened in this review. The 2026-2036 Kentucky Election Schedule was removed as a source because it does not cover this period.

The Fayette County Clerk official cumulative report for the May 19, 2026 primary lists a seven-candidate nonpartisan MAYOR contest (Linda Gorton 25298, Raquel E. Carter 15615, Greg O'Neal 5073, and four others). The primary only narrows the field. The decisive general election falls on the November 2026 date, after the September 14, 2026 cutoff. KRS 83A.040(1) sets a four-year mayoral term, which matches the 2022 election followed by the 2026 contest.
